records.literal_gloss: In the month the eighth, in year two of Darius, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah son of Berechiah son of Iddo the prophet, saying:

en.L: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
en.B: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
en.R: In the eighth month of the year, in Darius's second year as king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message to the prophet Zechariah. Zechariah was the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. This is the message:

es.L: En el mes octavo, en el año segundo de Darío, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido, el profeta, diciendo:
es.B: En el mes octavo del segundo año del reinado de Darío, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Zacarías, hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido:
es.R: En el octavo mes del año, en el segundo año de Darío como rey, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio un mensaje al profeta Zacarías. Zacarías era hijo de Berequías y nieto de Ido. Este es el mensaje:

fr.L: Le huitième mois, la deuxième année de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo, le prophète, disant :
fr.B: Le huitième mois de la deuxième année du règne de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée au prophète Zacharie, fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo :
fr.R: Le huitième mois de l’année, la deuxième année où Darius était roi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un message au prophète Zacharie. Zacharie était le fils de Bérékia et le petit-fils d’Iddo. Voici ce message :

sw.L: Katika mwezi wa nane, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido, nabii, kusema:
sw.B: Katika mwezi wa nane wa mwaka wa pili wa utawala wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia nabii Zekaria, mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido:
sw.R: Katika mwezi wa nane wa mwaka, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario kuwa mfalme, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa nabii Zekaria ujumbe. Zekaria alikuwa mwana wa Berekia na mjukuu wa Ido. Huu ndio ujumbe:

vi.L: Vào tháng thứ tám, năm thứ hai đời Đa-ri-út, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, con trai Y-đô, là nhà tiên tri, rằng:
vi.B: Vào tháng tám năm thứ hai triều vua Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri, con trai Bê-rê-kia, cháu Y-đô:
vi.R: Vào tháng tám năm ấy, năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri một sứ điệp. Xa-cha-ri là con trai Bê-rê-kia và là cháu Y-đô. Sứ điệp ấy như sau:

ko.L: 여덟째 달, 다리오 제2년에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 여덟째 달에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임했다.
ko.R: 다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 여덟째 달에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예언자 스가랴에게 말씀을 주셨다. 스가랴는 베레갸의 아들이고 잇도의 손자였다. 그 말씀은 이러하다.

decisions.choice: the eighth month of the second year of Darius: October to November 520 BC
decisions.reason: Darius I was king of Persia from 522 to 486 BC, and Judah was a small province of his empire. The months are counted from the spring, so the eighth month fell in the autumn; it began late in October 520 BC. No day is given. Zechariah's first message came two months after Haggai's first (Haggai 1:1, the sixth month of the same year), in the weeks between Haggai's messages of the seventh and the ninth months (Haggai 2:1, 10). The work on the temple had begun again about two months before (Haggai 1:14-15). The modern date is worked out from the Babylonian calendar, which the Jews used after the exile.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo: a prophet among the exiles who came back from Babylon
decisions.reason: Ezra names Haggai and Zechariah as the two prophets who urged the people to rebuild the temple (Ezra 5:1; 6:14). There Zechariah is called "son of Iddo", using "son" for a descendant, as Hebrew often does; here his father Berechiah is named as well. Nehemiah 12:4 and 16 list Iddo as the head of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel, and a Zechariah as its head in the next generation, so the prophet was most likely a priest as well. His name means "the LORD remembers".

decisions.choice: the prophet: Zechariah's title
decisions.reason: The title stands at the end of the line of names, so it could go with Iddo, the last name. But the book is about Zechariah's prophecy, the same heading returns in verse 7, and Ezra 5:1 calls Zechariah a prophet.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Berechiah in Matthew 23:35
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the blood of "Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar" (Matthew 23:35). The killing of a Zechariah in the temple court is told of Zechariah son of Jehoiada in 2 Chronicles 24:20-22. Readers have explained Matthew's wording in more than one way. This book says nothing about how the prophet Zechariah died.

decisions.choice: in the second year of Darius (L); of Darius's reign (B); in Darius's second year as king (R); the word of the LORD came to (L, B); gave a message to (R)
decisions.reason: The date keeps the Hebrew form, as set for Haggai and Zechariah: "the second year of Darius's reign" at Balanced and "Darius's second year as king" at Readable, as in Jeremiah's dated headings. Readable says "of the year" for the month but does not change the date into the modern calendar; the decision above gives it. The heading formula follows the table for "the word of the LORD came to". Readable puts the names in a sentence of their own and says "grandson", since Iddo was Berechiah's father.

decisions.choice: "vino la palabra del SEÑOR a" (L), "la palabra del SEÑOR vino a" (B), "el SEÑOR le dio un mensaje a" (R); "en el año segundo de Darío" (L), "del reinado de Darío" (B), "de Darío como rey" (R); "Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido"
decisions.reason: The heading and the date follow the Spanish formulas set for Haggai and Zechariah (Jeremiah 1:1-2), with no modern calendar date in the text. Names are the published forms: Darío, Zacarías hijo de Ido (Ezra 5:1), Berequías as in Chronicles, although Matthew 23:35 has "Baraquías" from the Greek.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}", with article and preposition inside the span; tú to the prophet, and plural_you on every "you" addressed to the people
decisions.reason: Book-wide for Zechariah: the divine name follows the Spanish prophets. God speaks to Zechariah, and the angels to him, with tú; Zechariah's hearers are always plural, so every plural "you", verbs and possessives included, takes the plural_you setting (ustedes by default, vosotros as the alternative).

decisions.choice: "la parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à" (L, B), "le SEIGNEUR a donné un message à" (R); "la deuxième année de Darius" (L), "du règne de Darius" (B), "où Darius était roi" (R); "Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d'Iddo"
decisions.reason: The heading follows Jeremiah 1:1-2 and the dates of Haggai and Zechariah at each level, with no modern date in the text. The names are those of the French term sheet for the Twelve: Darius, Zacharie, Bérékia, Iddo.

decisions.choice: narrative in the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R: the dated headings, Zechariah's night visions (1:7-6:8), the delegation of 7:1-3 and the prophet's own story (11:7-17); the LORD's words and the oracles in the present, future and passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: Book-wide for Zechariah: the dated headings and the first-person accounts ("je vis", "il me dit") are written narrative; what God, the angels and the prophet say is speech, so even the past told inside an oracle (7:11-14; 8:9) takes the passé composé. The first record of each narrative block also notes it. The divine name is "{{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}" throughout.

decisions.choice: "neno la BWANA likamjia" (L), "lilimjia" (B), "BWANA alimpa ... ujumbe" (R); "mwaka wa pili wa Dario" (L), "wa utawala wa Dario" (B), "wa Dario kuwa mfalme" (R); "Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido"
decisions.reason: The heading and date formulas of the Swahili prophets (Jeremiah 1:1-2; Haggai). Zekaria keeps the Old Testament form of Ezra 5:1, kept apart from Matthew 23:35's "Zakaria mwana wa Barakia", which follows the Greek.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}"; deity_pronoun only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: Book-wide for Zechariah, as in the Swahili prophets: BWANA is the divine-name setting with Yahwe as the alternative, and God's pronoun setting goes only on free words such as "kwangu", "yangu", "wangu", never on a verb prefix or object marker.

decisions.choice: "năm thứ hai đời Đa-ri-út" (L), "triều vua Đa-ri-út" (B), "Đa-ri-út làm vua" (R); "Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, con trai Y-đô" (L), "cháu Y-đô" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The dated heading follows the Vietnamese date formula for Haggai and Zechariah, with no modern date in the text. Literal keeps the Hebrew's two "son of"; Balanced and Readable say "cháu" (grandson), as the English Readable does. "Xa-cha-ri" and "Y-đô" are the published forms (Ezra 5:1).

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) to Zechariah and "các ngươi" to the people; to Zion and Jerusalem he says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B) / "con" or "các con" (R) in promises and "ngươi" at every level in judgment; the angels say "tôi" and "ông" to Zechariah, and he answers "thưa chúa tôi" (L, B) / "thưa ngài" (R); the angel of the LORD says "ta" and "ngươi" to Joshua (3:4), while the LORD's message to Joshua takes "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide address for Zechariah, as in the Vietnamese prophets (God speaks tenderly to Zion with "con", as in Zephaniah 3:14-20). Zechariah 9:9-10 keep "Vua của ngươi" (L, B) / "Vua của các ngươi" (R), the words Matthew 21:5 quotes. God's own "Ta" and "Ngài" in mid-sentence take the deity_pronoun setting; the angels never do.

decisions.choice: "잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴"; "다리오 제2년" (L), "다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해" (B), "다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해" (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows the term sheet at every level (Ezra 5:1 calls him 잇도의 아들 스가랴, using "son" for grandson); the dates follow the Kings formula, with months in words and the year in figures.

decisions.choice: narration in the plain style with -시- for God (스가랴 says 나); God speaks 해라체 and never takes -시- in his own mouth; the angel speaks 해라체 and Zechariah answers in 합쇼체, calling him 내 주여; the angel of the LORD speaks to Joshua in 해라체; the prophet speaks to people in his own voice in 하오체 (11:12)
decisions.reason: Book-wide speech levels for Zechariah, as the term sheet sets them for the prophets' visions. Korean has no deity_pronoun spans.

records.literal_gloss: Was angry Yahweh with your fathers [with] anger.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with your fathers with [great] anger.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with your ancestors.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with your ancestors.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó con {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} con [gran] enojo.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estuvo muy enojado con {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est irrité contre vos pères d’une [grande] irritation.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a été très irrité contre vos ancêtres.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a été très en colère contre vos ancêtres.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã nổi giận với tổ phụ các ngươi bằng cơn giận [lớn].
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã rất giận tổ tiên các ngươi.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã nổi giận rất nhiều với tổ tiên các ngươi.

decisions.choice: angry with anger: very angry
decisions.reason: The verb is followed by its own noun, "was angry ... anger", a Hebrew way of making a statement strong. The anger is past: it fell on the generations before the exile, and verse 15 calls it a little anger compared with the anger the LORD now feels toward the nations.

decisions.choice: your fathers: your ancestors, the generations before the exile
decisions.reason: "Fathers" is used for forebears in general. The ancestors of Zechariah's hearers were the people of Judah whose sins brought the fall of Jerusalem and the exile (2 Kings 24:3-4; 2 Chronicles 36:15-16). "Your" is plural: the people of Zechariah's own day are addressed.

decisions.choice: fathers (L); ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah, Literal keeps "fathers" and the other levels say "ancestors", which is what the word means here and includes mothers as well. Literal shows the strengthening with the bracketed "great"; the other levels say "very angry".

decisions.choice: "se enojó ... con [gran] enojo"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb with its own noun, as the Hebrew does, and brackets the strengthening the English Literal shows; "sus padres" with plural_you, since the people are addressed.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 ... 진노하였다", without -시-
decisions.reason: The verse is the LORD's own word to the people, so the LORD speaks of himself without the honorific, as the term sheet sets for God's own mouth.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלַ֔י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְאָשׁ֣וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to them, Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Return to me, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, and I will return to you, says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: So say to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, that I may return to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts."
en.B: So tell them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and I will return to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."
en.R: So tell the people, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and I will come back to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."

es.L: Así que diles: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, para que yo vuelva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos».
es.B: Así que diles: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, y yo volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos».
es.R: Así que dile al pueblo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, y yo volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos».

fr.L: Dis-leur donc : « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, pour que je revienne vers vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. »
fr.B: Dis-leur donc : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, et je reviendrai vers vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. »
fr.R: Dis donc au peuple : « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, et je reviendrai vers vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. »

sw.L: Basi, uwaambie, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Rudini {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, ili {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} niwarudie ninyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."
sw.B: Basi, waambie, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Rudini {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawarudia ninyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."
sw.R: Basi, waambie watu, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Rudini {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitarudi kwenu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi."

vi.L: Vậy ngươi hãy nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy trở lại cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy, để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trở lại cùng các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."
vi.B: Vậy con hãy nói với họ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy trở lại cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại cùng các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."
vi.R: Vậy con hãy nói với dân chúng: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ quay về với các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán."

ko.L: 그러므로 너는 그들에게 말하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희는 나에게로 돌아오너라. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 그러면 나도 너희에게로 돌아가겠다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."
ko.B: 그러므로 그들에게 말하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희는 나에게 돌아오너라. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그러면 나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."
ko.R: 그러므로 백성에게 말하여라. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 나에게 돌아오너라. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그러면 나도 너희에게 돌아가겠다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."

decisions.choice: return to me, and I will return to you: the people's turning and God's turning toward them in favor
decisions.reason: The same verb is used both ways. For the people it means turning away from their evil ways back to the LORD (verse 4); for the LORD it means turning back to them with favor after the years of anger. Malachi 3:7 repeats the call almost word for word, and verse 16 says that the LORD has returned to Jerusalem. The order of the sentence calls the people to turn, and promises that God will meet them.

decisions.choice: say to them: a command to the prophet about the people of his day
decisions.reason: The verb form is the one Hebrew uses to carry on a command, so "you will say" means "say". "Them" are the people of Zechariah's day, whose ancestors were named in verse 2.

decisions.choice: three formulas in one verse: the message is the LORD's own word
decisions.reason: The verse names the LORD of hosts three times, with "thus says", "declares" and "says". The Hebrew uses two different words: the first and last are the ordinary verb "says"; the middle one is the noun used for a solemn declaration. Piling them up stresses that the call to return comes from the LORD himself. On the title "the LORD of hosts", which runs through Zechariah, see the note at Isaiah 1:9.

decisions.choice: Thus says ... declares ... says the LORD of hosts (L); The LORD of Armies says this ... declares ... says (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says ... says ... says (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas follow the wording set for the prophets: "declares the LORD" for the solemn declaration, "says the LORD" for the plain verb, and "the LORD of hosts" at Literal and "the LORD of Armies" at the other levels. Readable says "says" for both, as the table sets, and "come back" for "return". Literal says "that I may return", since the Hebrew joins the promise to the call with a simple "and" that can express purpose. The words Zechariah is to speak stand in double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR de los ejércitos" (L), "de los Ejércitos" (B, R); "declara" (L), "afirma" (B), "dice" (R) for the solemn formula, "dice" for the plain verb; "vuelvan ... volveré"
decisions.reason: The formulas of the Spanish prophets, kept through the book. The same verb "volver" is used for the people's turning and for the LORD's, as the Hebrew uses one verb both ways (m1).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level; "déclare" (L, B) / "dit" (R) for the solemn formula, "dit" for the plain verb; "Revenez à moi ... je reviendrai vers vous"
decisions.reason: French keeps "le SEIGNEUR des armées" where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies", as the published prophets and Psalms do. "Revenir" is used both for the people and for God, keeping the one Hebrew verb (m1).

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level; "Rudini kwangu ... nami nitawarudia"
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level, as the published prophets, and one verb "kurudi" for the people's turning and the LORD's, as the Hebrew does (m1).

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" for the plain verb at every level, "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán vậy" (L, B) for the solemn formula; "trở lại cùng Ta" (L, B), "quay về với Ta" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "phán vậy" for the solemn declaration and "phán" for the plain "says" in Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi. The one verb is used both for the people and for God (m1). God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) to the prophet.

decisions.choice: "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L), "이렇게 말씀하신다" (B), "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 ... 하시는 말씀이다" (R); "의 선언이다" (L) for the solemn formula; "가 말한다" for the plain verb, with 거느린 in God's own mouth (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas of the Korean prophets: "Thus says" keeps the honorific, the closing formulas are God's own words and have none.

source.text: אַל־תִּהְי֣וּ כַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרְאֽוּ־אֲלֵיהֶם֩ הַנְּבִיאִ֨ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֤וּבוּ נָא֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֔ים וּמַֽעֲלְלֵיכֶ֖םהָֽרָעִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֛וּ וְלֹֽא־הִקְשִׁ֥יבוּ אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be like your fathers, to whom called the prophets the former, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Turn back now from your ways evil and your deeds evil; and not they listened and not they paid attention to me, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets called out, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Turn back, please, from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they did not listen, and they did not pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the earlier prophets called out, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Turn back from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they would not listen or pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Do not be like your ancestors. Long ago the prophets called out to them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Turn away from the evil way you live and the evil things you do." But your ancestors would not listen. They paid no attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}, a quienes clamaron los profetas antiguos, diciendo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} ahora de {{plural_you:sus malos caminos|vuestros malos caminos}} y de {{plural_you:sus malas obras|vuestras malas obras}}». Pero no escucharon, ni {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} prestaron atención, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, a quienes los profetas de antes proclamaron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} de {{plural_you:sus malos caminos|vuestros malos caminos}} y de {{plural_you:sus malas obras|vuestras malas obras}}». Pero no quisieron escuchar ni {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} hicieron caso, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}. Hace mucho tiempo los profetas les gritaban: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de la mala manera en que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} y de las cosas malas que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}». Pero {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} no quisieron escuchar. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} hicieron ningún caso, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Ne soyez pas comme vos pères, auxquels les premiers prophètes ont crié, disant : « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez donc de vos mauvaises voies et de vos mauvaises actions. » Mais ils n’ont pas écouté, et ils n’ont pas été attentifs à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ne soyez pas comme vos ancêtres, à qui les prophètes d’autrefois ont lancé cet appel : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Revenez de vos mauvaises voies et de vos mauvaises actions. » Mais ils n’ont voulu ni écouter ni faire attention à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ne soyez pas comme vos ancêtres. Il y a longtemps, les prophètes leur ont crié : « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Revenez, quittez votre mauvaise conduite et le mal que vous faites. » Mais vos ancêtres n’ont pas voulu écouter. Ils n’ont fait aucune attention à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Msiwe kama baba zenu, ambao manabii wa kwanza waliwalilia, wakisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Rudini sasa kutoka katika njia zenu mbaya na matendo yenu mabaya." Lakini hawakusikia, wala hawakunisikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Msiwe kama babu zenu, ambao manabii wa zamani waliwaita, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Rudini, acheni njia zenu mbaya na matendo yenu mabaya." Lakini hawakutaka kusikia wala kunisikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Msiwe kama babu zenu. Zamani manabii waliwaita, wakisema, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Rudini, acheni maisha yenu mabaya na mambo mabaya mnayofanya." Lakini babu zenu hawakutaka kusikiliza. Hawakunijali hata kidogo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Chớ như tổ phụ các ngươi, là những người mà các nhà tiên tri thuở trước đã kêu gọi rằng: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy quay lại đi, khỏi các đường lối gian ác và các việc làm gian ác của các ngươi." Nhưng chúng đã không nghe, cũng không chú ý đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Đừng như tổ tiên các ngươi, là những người mà các nhà tiên tri thuở trước đã kêu gọi: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy quay lại, từ bỏ đường lối gian ác và việc làm gian ác của các ngươi." Nhưng chúng không chịu nghe, cũng chẳng để ý đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Đừng như tổ tiên các ngươi. Từ lâu, các nhà tiên tri đã kêu gọi chúng: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy quay lại, từ bỏ lối sống gian ác và những việc ác các ngươi làm." Nhưng tổ tiên các ngươi không chịu nghe. Chúng chẳng để ý gì đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 너희는 너희 조상들처럼 되지 말아라. 이전 예언자들이 그들에게 외쳐 말하기를 "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희는 너희의 악한 길과 너희의 악한 행실에서 제발 돌아오너라" 하였으나, 그들은 듣지 않았고 나에게 귀를 기울이지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 너희 조상들처럼 되지 말아라. 이전 예언자들이 그들에게 "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희의 악한 길과 악한 행실에서 돌아오너라" 하고 외쳤다. 그러나 그들은 듣지도 않고 나에게 귀를 기울이지도 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희 조상들처럼 되지 말아라. 오래전에 예언자들이 그들에게 외쳤다. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 악하게 사는 길에서 돌아오고, 악한 일을 그만두어라." 그러나 너희 조상들은 들으려 하지 않았다. 그들은 내 말에 조금도 귀를 기울이지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: the former prophets: the prophets before the exile, and their call to turn back
decisions.reason: The earlier prophets are those who spoke before Jerusalem fell. Their call is summed up in words very close to Jeremiah's: "Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and your evil deeds" (Jeremiah 25:5; compare 18:11; 35:15), and 2 Kings 17:13 sums up the message of all the prophets the same way. Zechariah sets his message in line with theirs.

decisions.choice: please: a small word that softens a command into an appeal
decisions.reason: The word is often left untranslated. Here it makes "turn back" a plea as well as an order: the prophets begged the people to turn.

decisions.choice: and your deeds: the form the Hebrew text tells the reader to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text and the form marked to be read aloud differ slightly in spelling here. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: they did not listen ... did not pay attention: the ancestors refused the call
decisions.reason: The two verbs are a pair that Jeremiah often uses for Judah's refusal (Jeremiah 6:10; 7:24, 26). The LORD speaks of himself as "me": the prophets' words were his words.

decisions.choice: please (L); not shown (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable let the tone of the sentence carry the plea; an added "please" would sound weak in a command from God. Readable says "the evil way you live" for "your evil ways", and names the ancestors again for clarity.

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} ahora"
decisions.reason: The small word of entreaty is given as "ahora", the usual way of carrying it in a Spanish plea; "por favor" would sound casual in the prophets' call. The ancestors were a group, so the prophets' words to them take plural_you too.

decisions.choice: "제발 돌아오너라"
decisions.reason: Literal shows the softening word of the plea with 제발; Balanced and Readable leave it to the tone, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: Your fathers, where [are] they? And the prophets, forever do they live?

en.L: Your fathers, where [are] they? And the prophets, will they live forever?
en.B: Your ancestors, where are they now? And the prophets, do they live forever?
en.R: Where are your ancestors now? And did the prophets live forever?

es.R: ¿Dónde están ahora {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}? ¿Y acaso los profetas vivieron para siempre?

vi.R: Tổ tiên các ngươi bây giờ ở đâu? Các nhà tiên tri có sống mãi được đâu?

ko.B: 너희 조상들, 그들이 지금 어디 있느냐? 예언자들은 영원히 사느냐?
ko.R: 너희 조상들이 지금 어디 있느냐? 예언자들이 영원히 살았느냐?

decisions.choice: two questions that need no answer: both generations have died
alternatives: the people's reply, that the prophets are dead too
decisions.reason: The ancestors are gone, carried off by the judgment the prophets warned of. The prophets were mortal as well. The point comes in verse 6: people die, but the LORD's words did not die with them; they caught up with the ancestors. A few readers take the second question as the hearers' answer back to the prophet ("and the prophets, are they still alive?"), but nothing marks a change of speaker.

decisions.choice: Where are your ancestors now? And did the prophets live forever?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the questions in ordinary order. Its second question looks back to the earlier prophets, which is what the Hebrew means.

source.text: אַ֣ךְ׀דְּבָרַ֣י וְחֻקַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים הֲל֥וֹא הִשִּׂ֖יגוּ אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר זָמַ֜ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔נוּ כִּדְרָכֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּכְמַ֣עֲלָלֵ֔ינוּ כֵּ֖ן עָשָׂ֥ה אִתָּֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But my words and my statutes which I commanded my servants the prophets, did not they overtake your fathers? And they repented and said, Just as planned Yahweh of hosts to do to us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so he has done with us.

en.L: Yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I commanded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, have they not overtaken your fathers? Then they turned back and said, "Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts purposed to deal with us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has dealt with us."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} decrees, the ones I commanded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to speak, did they not catch up with your ancestors? Then they repented and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has dealt with us as our ways and our deeds deserved, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to do."
en.R: But the words and the laws that I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to speak, did they not catch up with your ancestors? Then they turned back and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has done to us what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to do. He has punished us for the way we lived and for the things we did."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos que mandé a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}? Entonces se volvieron y dijeron: «Como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos se propuso hacer con nosotros, conforme a nuestros caminos y conforme a nuestras obras, así lo ha hecho con nosotros».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} decretos, los que mandé anunciar a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}? Entonces se volvieron a Dios y dijeron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos nos ha tratado como merecían nuestros caminos y nuestras obras, tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo había propuesto».
es.R: Pero las palabras y las leyes que di a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} siervos los profetas para que las anunciaran, ¿no alcanzaron a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}? Entonces ellos se volvieron a Dios y dijeron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos nos ha hecho lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había planeado hacer. Nos ha castigado por la manera en que vivimos y por las cosas que hicimos».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions, que j’avais ordonnées à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes, n’ont-elles pas atteint vos pères ? Alors ils sont revenus et ont dit : « Comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait projeté d’agir envers nous, selon nos voies et selon nos actions, ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a agi envers nous. »
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} décrets, ceux que j’avais ordonné à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes d’annoncer, n’ont-ils pas rattrapé vos ancêtres ? Alors ils sont revenus à Dieu et ont dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées nous a traités comme le méritaient nos voies et nos actions, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait projeté. »
fr.R: Mais les paroles et les lois que j’ai données à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} serviteurs les prophètes pour qu’ils les annoncent, n’ont-elles pas rattrapé vos ancêtres ? Alors ils sont revenus à Dieu et ont dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées nous a fait ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait prévu de faire. Il nous a punis pour notre façon de vivre et pour ce que nous avons fait. »

sw.L: Lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, niliyowaamuru watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii, je, hayakuwapata baba zenu? Ndipo wakarudi, wakasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alivyokusudia kututendea, kwa kadiri ya njia zetu na kwa kadiri ya matendo yetu, ndivyo alivyotutendea."
sw.B: Lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na maagizo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, yale niliyowaamuru watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii wayatangaze, je, hayakuwakuta babu zenu? Ndipo wakamrudia Mungu, wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ametutendea kama njia zetu na matendo yetu yalivyostahili, kama alivyokusudia kufanya."
sw.R: Lakini maneno na sheria nilizowapa watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manabii ili wazitangaze, je, hazikuwakuta babu zenu? Ndipo wakamrudia Mungu, wakasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ametufanyia kile alichokusudia kufanya. Ametuadhibu kwa sababu ya jinsi tulivyoishi na mambo tuliyofanya."

vi.L: Nhưng các lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và các luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các nhà tiên tri, há chẳng đã đuổi kịp tổ phụ các ngươi sao? Bấy giờ chúng quay lại và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã định xử với chúng tôi thế nào, theo đường lối chúng tôi và theo việc làm chúng tôi, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã xử với chúng tôi thể ấy."
vi.B: Nhưng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và các mạng lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là những điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các nhà tiên tri rao báo, chẳng phải đã đuổi kịp tổ tiên các ngươi sao? Bấy giờ chúng quay về và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã xử với chúng tôi đúng như đường lối và việc làm của chúng tôi đáng phải chịu, y như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định."
vi.R: Nhưng những lời và luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho các đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là các nhà tiên tri để họ rao truyền, chẳng phải đã đuổi kịp tổ tiên các ngươi sao? Khi ấy chúng ăn năn quay về và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã làm cho chúng tôi điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định. Ngài đã phạt chúng tôi vì cách chúng tôi sống và những việc chúng tôi làm."

ko.L: 그러나 내가 내 종 예언자들에게 명령한 내 말과 내 규례가 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그러자 그들이 돌아와서 말하였다. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리의 길대로, 우리의 행실대로 우리에게 행하시려고 계획하신 그대로 우리에게 행하셨다."
ko.B: 그러나 내가 내 종 예언자들에게 전하라고 명령한 내 말과 내 규례가 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그러자 그들이 돌아와서 말했다. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리의 길과 행실에 마땅한 대로 우리를 대하셨다. 그분께서 계획하신 그대로다."
ko.R: 내가 내 종 예언자들에게 전하게 한 말과 법이 너희 조상들을 따라잡지 않았느냐? 그때 그들은 돌아와서 말했다. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 계획하신 대로 우리에게 하셨다. 우리가 살아온 방식과 우리가 한 일 때문에 우리를 벌하셨다."

decisions.choice: overtake: catch up with someone, as a pursuer does
decisions.reason: The verb is used in the covenant warnings: if the people do not obey, "all these curses will come on you and overtake you" (Deuteronomy 28:15, 45). The prophets died, but the words they spoke kept on running and caught the ancestors.

decisions.choice: they repented: the ancestors, when the judgment fell
alternatives: the people of Zechariah's day, who answered his call
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is "your fathers", and the sentence reads most naturally as their confession after the disaster came, like the prayers of the exiles (Lamentations 2:17; Daniel 9:11-14). It can also be read as a report of how Zechariah's own hearers responded to verses 3-5, as the people answered Haggai (Haggai 1:12). The verse does not settle it.

decisions.choice: just as the LORD purposed to do: the judgment was what God had planned and warned of
decisions.reason: Lamentations 2:17 makes the same confession with the same verb: "The LORD has done what he purposed; he has carried out his word." The disaster was not chance: God did what he said he would do, and he did it in keeping with what the people had done.

decisions.choice: statutes: the decrees God laid down
decisions.reason: The word means something fixed by decree. Joined with "words", it covers both the warnings and the laws the prophets were sent to press on the people.

decisions.choice: The LORD of Armies has dealt with us as our ways and our deeds deserved (B); He has punished us for the way we lived (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main clause first, which English finds easier. Readable says "punished us", which is what "dealt with us according to our ways" means here, and "statutes" becomes "laws".

decisions.choice: "se volvieron a Dios"
decisions.reason: The verb is the "return" of verses 3-4, and the Spanish prophets render it with "volver", never "arrepentirse"; Balanced and Readable add "a Dios" to say where they turned.

decisions.choice: "ils sont revenus à Dieu"
decisions.reason: French keeps "revenir" for this verb at every level, so the turning of the ancestors echoes the call of verses 3-4; Balanced and Readable say to whom they turned.

source.text: בְּיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לְעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ שְׁבָ֔ט בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔הוּ בֶּן־עִדּ֥וֹא הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: On day twenty and four of the eleventh month, it [is the] month of Shebat, in year two of Darius, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah son of Berechiah son of Iddo the prophet, saying:

en.L: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, that is, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
en.B: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, the eleventh month, in the second year of Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
en.R: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, the eleventh month of the year, in Darius's second year as king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave another message to the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo. This is the message:

es.L: El día veinticuatro del mes undécimo, que es el mes de Sebat, en el año segundo de Darío, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido, el profeta, diciendo:
es.B: El día veinticuatro de Sebat, el mes undécimo, en el segundo año del reinado de Darío, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Zacarías, hijo de Berequías, hijo de Ido:
es.R: El día veinticuatro de Sebat, el undécimo mes del año, en el segundo año de Darío como rey, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio otro mensaje al profeta Zacarías, hijo de Berequías y nieto de Ido. Este es el mensaje:

fr.L: Le vingt-quatrième jour du onzième mois, c’est-à-dire le mois de Shebat, la deuxième année de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo, le prophète, disant :
fr.B: Le vingt-quatrième jour de Shebat, le onzième mois, la deuxième année du règne de Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée au prophète Zacharie, fils de Bérékia, fils d’Iddo :
fr.R: Le vingt-quatrième jour de Shebat, le onzième mois de l’année, la deuxième année où Darius était roi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un autre message au prophète Zacharie, le fils de Bérékia et le petit-fils d’Iddo. Voici ce message :

sw.L: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya mwezi wa kumi na moja, yaani, mwezi wa Shebati, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia Zekaria mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido, nabii, kusema:
sw.B: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya Shebati, mwezi wa kumi na moja, katika mwaka wa pili wa utawala wa Dario, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia nabii Zekaria, mwana wa Berekia, mwana wa Ido:
sw.R: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya Shebati, mwezi wa kumi na moja wa mwaka, katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario kuwa mfalme, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa nabii Zekaria, mwana wa Berekia na mjukuu wa Ido, ujumbe mwingine. Huu ndio ujumbe:

vi.L: Vào ngày hai mươi bốn tháng thứ mười một, tức là tháng Sê-bát, năm thứ hai đời Đa-ri-út, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Xa-cha-ri con trai Bê-rê-kia, con trai Y-đô, là nhà tiên tri, rằng:
vi.B: Ngày hai mươi bốn tháng Sê-bát, tức tháng mười một, năm thứ hai triều vua Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri, con trai Bê-rê-kia, cháu Y-đô:
vi.R: Ngày hai mươi bốn tháng Sê-bát, tức tháng mười một trong năm, năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho nhà tiên tri Xa-cha-ri, con trai Bê-rê-kia và cháu Y-đô, một sứ điệp khác. Sứ điệp ấy như sau:

ko.L: 열한째 달 곧 스밧 월 이십사일, 다리오 제2년에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 열한째 달인 스밧 월 이십사일에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 잇도의 손자 베레갸의 아들 예언자 스가랴에게 임했다.
ko.R: 다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 열한째 달인 스밧 월 24일에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예언자 스가랴에게 또 말씀을 주셨다. 스가랴는 베레갸의 아들이고 잇도의 손자였다. 그 말씀은 이러하다.

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, Shebat, in Darius's second year: February 519 BC
decisions.reason: This is about the middle of February 519 BC, three months after verse 1. It is exactly two months after the day on which Haggai gave his last two messages (Haggai 2:10, 20), and five months after work on the temple began again (Haggai 1:15). Shebat is the Babylonian name of the month, which the Jews took up during the exile; this is its only use in the Bible.

decisions.choice: one heading for a series of visions in one night
decisions.reason: The heading speaks of Zechariah by name, and the report that follows speaks in his own voice: "I saw in the night" (verse 8). This one heading covers the eight night visions of 1:8-6:8, and the book gives no new date until 7:1. The visions are told as seen in a single night, though the text does not say so in so many words.

decisions.choice: the dated heading as in verse 1
decisions.reason: The date and the heading follow the wording of verse 1 at each level. Readable puts the month's name first and adds "another", since this is the second message.

decisions.choice: "Sebat"
decisions.reason: The Babylonian month name is new in Spanish; it takes the Spanish spelling pattern of the published names (s for sh, as "Sesbasar"). Literal keeps the Hebrew order, "del mes undécimo, que es el mes de Sebat".

decisions.choice: "le mois de Shebat"
decisions.reason: A new name in French, spelled with "sh" as the term sheet writes Hebrew names (Méshek, Shinéar).

decisions.choice: "mwezi wa Shebati"
decisions.reason: A new name; it takes the usual Swahili pattern, a final -i after the closed syllable, with "sh" kept.

decisions.choice: "tháng Sê-bát"
decisions.reason: A new name in Vietnamese, transliterated in the Protestant pattern; days up to ten take "mồng", so the twenty-fourth day has none.

decisions.choice: "스밧 월"; "이십사일" (L, B), "24일" (R)
decisions.reason: Shebat is written 스밧, the usual Protestant form, with 월 after it as Nehemiah 1:1 writes "기슬르 월" (Zechariah 7:1). Days are in words at Literal and Balanced ("이십사일", as Haggai 2:10) and in figures at Readable, as the Kings date formula.

source.text: רָאִ֣יתִי׀הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ רֹכֵב֙ עַל־ס֣וּס אָדֹ֔ם וְה֣וּא עֹמֵ֔ד בֵּ֥ין הַהֲדַסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמְּצֻלָ֑ה וְאַחֲרָיו֙ סוּסִ֣ים אֲדֻמִּ֔ים שְׂרֻקִּ֖ים וּלְבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: I saw the night, and look, a man riding on a horse red, and he [was] standing among the myrtles which [were] in the hollow, and behind him horses red, sorrel, and white.

en.L: I saw in the night, and look, a man riding on a red horse! And he was standing among the myrtles that [were] in the hollow, and behind him [were] horses, red, sorrel and white.
en.B: I saw a vision in the night: there was a man mounted on a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were red, sorrel and white horses.
en.R: During the night I saw a vision. A man was riding a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in a deep valley. Behind him were horses that were red, reddish brown and white.

es.L: Vi de noche, y he aquí un hombre montado sobre un caballo rojo; y él estaba de pie entre los mirtos que [había] en la hondonada, y detrás de él [había] caballos rojos, alazanes y blancos.
es.B: Tuve una visión de noche: vi a un hombre montado en un caballo rojo. Estaba de pie entre los mirtos de la quebrada, y detrás de él había caballos rojos, alazanes y blancos.
es.R: Durante la noche vi una visión. Un hombre iba montado en un caballo rojo. Estaba de pie entre los mirtos, en un valle profundo. Detrás de él había caballos rojos, castaños y blancos.

fr.L: Je vis pendant la nuit, et voici, un homme monté sur un cheval roux ! Il se tenait parmi les myrtes qui [étaient] dans le creux, et derrière lui [il y avait] des chevaux roux, alezans et blancs.
fr.B: J’eus une vision pendant la nuit : un homme était monté sur un cheval roux. Il se tenait parmi les myrtes du ravin, et derrière lui il y avait des chevaux roux, alezans et blancs.
fr.R: Pendant la nuit, j’ai eu une vision. Un homme était monté sur un cheval rouge. Il se tenait parmi les myrtes, au fond d’une vallée. Derrière lui, il y avait des chevaux rouges, brun-roux et blancs.

sw.L: Niliona usiku, na tazama, mtu amepanda farasi mwekundu! Naye alikuwa amesimama kati ya mihadasi iliyokuwa bondeni, na nyuma yake [walikuwa] farasi wekundu, wa kikahawia na weupe.
sw.B: Niliona maono usiku: palikuwa na mtu aliyepanda farasi mwekundu. Alisimama kati ya mihadasi bondeni, na nyuma yake kulikuwa na farasi wekundu, wa kikahawia na weupe.
sw.R: Usiku nilipata maono. Mtu mmoja alikuwa amepanda farasi mwekundu. Alikuwa amesimama kati ya miti ya mihadasi katika bonde lenye kina. Nyuma yake kulikuwa na farasi wekundu, wa rangi ya hudhurungi na weupe.

vi.L: Ban đêm tôi thấy, và kìa, một người cưỡi một con ngựa đỏ! Người ấy đang đứng giữa những cây sim ở chỗ trũng, và phía sau người ấy [có] những con ngựa đỏ, ngựa hồng nâu và ngựa trắng.
vi.B: Ban đêm tôi thấy một khải tượng: có một người cưỡi ngựa đỏ. Người ấy đứng giữa những cây sim trong khe núi, phía sau có những con ngựa đỏ, ngựa hồng nâu và ngựa trắng.
vi.R: Trong đêm, tôi thấy một khải tượng. Một người cưỡi một con ngựa đỏ. Người ấy đang đứng giữa những cây sim trong một thung lũng sâu. Phía sau người ấy có những con ngựa màu đỏ, màu nâu đỏ và màu trắng.

ko.L: 내가 밤에 보니, 보라, 한 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다! 그는 골짜기에 [있는] 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었고, 그 뒤에는 붉은 말과 밤색 말과 흰 말들이 [있었다].
ko.B: 내가 밤에 환상을 보았다. 한 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다. 그는 골짜기의 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었고, 그 뒤에는 붉은 말과 밤색 말과 흰 말들이 있었다.
ko.R: 밤에 나는 환상을 보았다. 어떤 사람이 붉은 말을 타고 있었다. 그는 깊은 골짜기에 있는 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있었다. 그의 뒤에는 붉은 말들과 붉은 갈색 말들과 흰 말들이 있었다.

decisions.choice: the first of eight night visions: horses that patrol the earth
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-6 report eight visions (1:8-17; 2:1-4; 2:5-17; 3:1-10; 4:1-14; 5:1-4; 5:5-11; 6:1-8). In each, Zechariah sees a picture, asks what it means, and an angel explains it. In this first one, riders who have gone throughout the earth report that it is quiet, and the LORD answers with comfort for Jerusalem. The book keeps the pictures as they were seen and lets the angel's words explain them; it does not say what each color means.

decisions.choice: the man on the red horse: the angel of the LORD of verse 11
decisions.reason: The man is described as "standing among the myrtle trees" in verses 8 and 10, and in verse 11 the same words are used of the angel of the LORD. So the rider is an angel in human form, the leader of the horsemen. He is not the angel who explains the visions (verse 9).

decisions.choice: myrtle trees: evergreen shrubs that grow near water
decisions.reason: The myrtle has dark, fragrant leaves and grows in damp, low places. Isaiah names it among the trees God will make grow when he restores his people (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13), and the returned exiles used its branches for the booths at the Festival of Booths (Nehemiah 8:15).

decisions.choice: in the hollow: a low, shaded place, a ravine or deep valley
alternatives: in the deep (a picture of the depths of the sea)
decisions.reason: The word is related to words for the depths of the sea (Exodus 15:5; Jonah 2:4) and is used here for a low place where myrtles grow. Some read it as a hint of the deep waters, others as a ravine near Jerusalem. The Greek translation reads "between the mountains", perhaps under the influence of 6:1. The sense of the scene does not depend on it.

decisions.choice: sorrel: reddish brown
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Isaiah 16:8 uses a related word for choice vines) and seems to name a reddish or brownish color. The colors of the horses are not explained in this vision; the riders are simply scouts sent out by the LORD (verse 10). Compare the colored horses of 6:2-3, which are partly different.

decisions.choice: look (L); there was (B); not shown (R); a vision (B, R); ravine (B), deep valley (R); reddish brown (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look", the word that marks something seen in a vision; Balanced says "there was", and Readable simply tells what he saw. Balanced and Readable add "a vision", which the whole passage makes plain. Readable says "reddish brown" for the rare color word.

decisions.choice: "Vi ..., y he aquí" (L), "Tuve una visión ... vi" (B), "vi una visión" (R); "mirtos"; "hondonada" (L), "quebrada" (B), "valle profundo" (R); "alazanes" (L, B), "castaños" (R)
decisions.reason: The vision formula of the Spanish prophets, at each level. The myrtle is "mirto" (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13); "alazán" is the usual word for a reddish-brown horse, and Readable uses the plainer "castaño", as the English Readable says "reddish brown".

decisions.choice: "les myrtes"; "le creux" (L), "le ravin" (B), "une vallée" (R); "roux ... alezans" (L, B), "rouges, brun-roux" (R)
decisions.reason: "Myrte" as Isaiah 41:19 and 55:13; "roux" and "alezan" are the words for a horse's coat, and Readable uses the plain colours, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "mihadasi"; "bondeni" (L, B), "bonde lenye kina" (R); "wa kikahawia" (L, B), "wa rangi ya hudhurungi" (R)
decisions.reason: "Mhadasi" is the Swahili name of the myrtle (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13; Nehemiah 8:15). The rare colour word is given as a brownish red.

decisions.choice: "những cây sim"; "chỗ trũng" (L), "khe núi" (B), "thung lũng sâu" (R); "ngựa hồng nâu" (L, B), "màu nâu đỏ" (R)
decisions.reason: "Cây sim" is the Vietnamese myrtle (Isaiah 41:19). Literal keeps "kìa" for the vision word; Balanced and Readable add "khải tượng", as the English adds "a vision".

decisions.choice: "화석류나무"; "밤색 말" (L, B), "붉은 갈색 말" (R)
decisions.reason: The myrtle keeps the Korean Bible's name 화석류 (Isaiah 41:19; 55:13); the modern botanical name 도금양 would be unfamiliar. The vision is narrated by Zechariah in the plain style with 나.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֖ר מָה־אֵ֣לֶּה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֔י אֲנִ֥י אַרְאֶ֖ךָּ מָה־הֵ֥מָּה אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, What [are] these, my lord? And said to me the angel who talks with me, I will show you what these [are].

en.L: And I said, "What [are] these, my lord?" And the angel who talked with me said to me, "I myself will show you what these are."
en.B: I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who talked with me answered, "I will show you what they are."
en.R: I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who talked with me said, "I will show you what they are."

es.L: Y dije: «¿Qué [son] estos, mi señor?». Y el ángel que hablaba conmigo me dijo: «Yo te mostraré qué son estos».
es.B: Pregunté: «¿Qué son estos, mi señor?». El ángel que hablaba conmigo respondió: «Yo te mostraré lo que son».
es.R: Pregunté: «¿Qué son estos, señor?». El ángel que hablaba conmigo me dijo: «Te mostraré lo que son».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Que [sont] ceux-ci, mon seigneur ? » Et l’ange qui parlait avec moi me dit : « C’est moi qui te montrerai ce que sont ceux-ci. »
fr.B: Je demandai : « Que sont-ils, mon seigneur ? » L’ange qui parlait avec moi répondit : « Je vais te montrer ce qu’ils sont. »
fr.R: J’ai demandé : « Qu’est-ce que c’est, mon seigneur ? » L’ange qui parlait avec moi m’a dit : « Je vais te montrer ce que c’est. »

sw.L: Nikasema, "Hawa ni nini, bwana wangu?" Naye malaika aliyezungumza nami akaniambia, "Mimi nitakuonyesha hawa ni nini."
sw.B: Nikauliza, "Bwana wangu, hawa ni nini?" Malaika aliyezungumza nami akajibu, "Nitakuonyesha hawa ni nini."
sw.R: Nikauliza, "Bwana wangu, hawa ni nini?" Malaika aliyezungumza nami akasema, "Nitakuonyesha maana yao."

vi.L: Tôi nói: "Thưa chúa tôi, những [vật] này là gì?" Và thiên sứ đang nói với tôi bảo tôi: "Chính tôi sẽ cho ông thấy những [vật] này là gì."
vi.B: Tôi hỏi: "Thưa chúa tôi, những điều này là gì?" Thiên sứ đang nói với tôi đáp: "Tôi sẽ cho ông biết những điều ấy là gì."
vi.R: Tôi hỏi: "Thưa ngài, những điều này là gì?" Thiên sứ đang nói với tôi bảo: "Tôi sẽ cho ông biết những điều ấy là gì."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 말하였다. "내 주여, 이것들이 무엇입니까?" 그러자 나와 말하던 천사가 나에게 말하였다. "이것들이 무엇인지 내가 너에게 보여 주겠다."
ko.B: 내가 물었다. "내 주여, 이것들이 무엇입니까?" 나와 말하던 천사가 대답했다. "이것들이 무엇인지 너에게 보여 주겠다."
ko.R: 내가 물었다. "내 주여, 이것들은 무엇입니까?" 나와 말하던 천사가 말했다. "그것들이 무엇인지 보여 주겠다."

decisions.choice: the angel who talked with me: the angel who explains the visions
alternatives: the angel who spoke in me
decisions.reason: The word for angel means a messenger, and here a heavenly one. This angel is Zechariah's guide through the visions: he answers his questions and explains what he sees, from this verse to 6:4. The small word after the verb usually means "with" when used with the verb "speak" (Numbers 12:8; Hosea 1:2); some take it as "in me", of a voice heard within. The same phrase is used for him each time he appears.

decisions.choice: my lord: a polite way of addressing someone of higher rank
decisions.reason: The word is used when speaking respectfully to a master, a king or a stranger of standing (Genesis 24:18; Judges 6:13). Zechariah uses it for the angel. It is not the word used for God.

decisions.choice: the angel who talked with me, at every level; my lord, lowercase
alternatives: the angel who spoke with me
decisions.reason: As set for Zechariah's visions, the angel keeps one description at every level and in every vision, so that the reader can follow him from scene to scene. "My lord" is lowercase because the angel is not God.

decisions.choice: "el ángel que hablaba conmigo"; "mi señor" (L, B), "señor" (R), lowercase, with tú
decisions.reason: One wording for the angel through all the visions, as the term sheet sets it; Zechariah addresses him politely but lowercase, since the angel is not God (m2).

decisions.choice: "l'ange qui parlait avec moi"; "mon seigneur", lowercase at every level; the angel says "tu" to Zechariah
decisions.reason: One description for the angel in every vision. French keeps "mon seigneur" even where the English Readable might be plainer, since "Seigneur" with a capital would read as God and "Monsieur" jars when said to an angel.

decisions.choice: "malaika aliyezungumza nami"; "bwana wangu", lowercase
decisions.reason: The angel keeps one description in every vision; "bwana wangu" is the polite address of a man to one above him and takes no span, since the angel is not God (m2).

decisions.choice: "thiên sứ đang nói với tôi"; "Thưa chúa tôi" (L, B), "Thưa ngài" (R); the angel says "tôi" and "ông"
decisions.reason: The angel keeps one description in every vision. Zechariah addresses him with the respectful "chúa tôi" for 'adoni, lowercase, as Joshua 5:14; Readable says "ngài". The angel speaks to the prophet as Gabriel speaks to Zechariah in Luke 1:13.

decisions.choice: "나와 말하던 천사"; "내 주여" with 합쇼체 from Zechariah; the angel answers in 해라체
decisions.reason: 내 주여 is kept for the angel at every level, and 주님 is kept for God. The angel's plain 해라체 matches the angels of Daniel.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַן הָאִ֛ישׁ הָעֹמֵ֥ד בֵּין־הַהַדַסִּ֖יםוַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה לְהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the man who [was] standing among the myrtles and said, These [are those] whom has sent Yahweh to go about in the earth.

en.L: And the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These [are those] whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent to walk about through the earth."
en.B: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees explained, "These are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent to patrol the earth."
en.R: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees said, "These are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent out to go all over the earth and see what is happening."

es.L: Y el hombre que estaba de pie entre los mirtos respondió y dijo: «Estos [son los] que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a recorrer la tierra».
es.B: Entonces el hombre que estaba de pie entre los mirtos explicó: «Estos son los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a patrullar la tierra».
es.R: Entonces el hombre que estaba entre los mirtos dijo: «Estos son los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado a recorrer toda la tierra para ver lo que pasa».

fr.L: Et l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes répondit et dit : « Ceux-ci [sont ceux] que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés pour parcourir la terre. »
fr.B: Alors l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes expliqua : « Ce sont ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés patrouiller sur la terre. »
fr.R: Alors l’homme qui se tenait parmi les myrtes a dit : « Ce sont ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a envoyés parcourir toute la terre pour voir ce qui s’y passe. »

sw.L: Naye yule mtu aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi akajibu, akasema, "Hawa [ndio] wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kutembea huku na huko duniani."
sw.B: Ndipo yule mtu aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi akaeleza, "Hawa ndio wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kuikagua dunia."
sw.R: Ndipo yule mtu aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi akasema, "Hawa ndio wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatuma kwenda kila mahali duniani ili waone yanayotendeka."

vi.L: Và người đang đứng giữa những cây sim đáp lời rằng: "Đây [là những người] mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi qua đi lại trên đất."
vi.B: Bấy giờ người đang đứng giữa những cây sim giải thích: "Đây là những người {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi tuần tra khắp đất."
vi.R: Bấy giờ người đứng giữa những cây sim nói: "Đây là những người {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đi khắp thế giới để xem mọi việc thế nào."

ko.L: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 대답하여 말하였다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 땅을 두루 다니라고 보내신 [자들이다]."
ko.B: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 설명했다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 땅을 순찰하라고 보내신 자들이다."
ko.R: 그러자 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있던 사람이 말했다. "이들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 땅을 돌아다니며 무슨 일이 일어나는지 살펴보라고 보내신 이들이다."

decisions.choice: to walk about through the earth: to go to and fro over it, like scouts on patrol
decisions.reason: The verb means to walk back and forth. It is used of the satan who has been "walking about" on the earth before he reports to the LORD (Job 1:7; 2:2), and of the horses that are sent out in 6:7. The riders are like a king's mounted scouts, who ride through his lands and bring back word.

decisions.choice: the man answers the question Zechariah put to the angel
decisions.reason: Zechariah asked the angel who talked with him (verse 9), but the answer comes from the rider among the myrtles. The angel's promise, "I will show you", is kept as the scene unfolds.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole world
decisions.reason: The same word means "land" or "earth". In verse 11 "all the earth" is at rest, and in verse 15 the LORD speaks of the nations, so the patrol covers the whole world.

decisions.choice: patrol (B); go all over the earth and see what is happening (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word for what the riders do; Readable spells out the purpose of the patrol, which the report in verse 11 shows.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ אֶת־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה הָֽעֹמֵד֙ בֵּ֣ין הַהֲדַסִּ֔ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת וְשֹׁקָֽטֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they answered the angel of Yahweh, who [was] standing among the myrtles, and said, We have gone about in the earth, and look, all the earth sits and [is] quiet.

en.L: And they answered the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one standing among the myrtles, and said, "We have walked about through the earth, and look, all the earth sits still and [is] at rest."
en.B: They reported to the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who stood among the myrtle trees: "We have patrolled the whole earth, and all of it is still and at rest."
en.R: They told the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who stood among the myrtle trees, "We have gone all over the earth. The whole world is calm and quiet."

es.L: Y ellos respondieron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el que estaba de pie entre los mirtos, y dijeron: «Hemos recorrido la tierra, y he aquí, toda la tierra está quieta y [está] en reposo».
es.B: Ellos informaron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que estaba de pie entre los mirtos: «Hemos patrullado toda la tierra, y toda ella está quieta y en reposo».
es.R: Le dijeron al ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que estaba de pie entre los mirtos: «Hemos recorrido toda la tierra. El mundo entero está en calma y tranquilo».

fr.L: Et ils répondirent à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, celui qui se tenait parmi les myrtes, et dirent : « Nous avons parcouru la terre, et voici, toute la terre demeure immobile et [est] en repos. »
fr.B: Ils firent leur rapport à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui se tenait parmi les myrtes : « Nous avons patrouillé sur toute la terre, et elle est tout entière tranquille et en repos. »
fr.R: Ils ont dit à l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui se tenait parmi les myrtes : « Nous avons parcouru toute la terre. Le monde entier est calme et paisible. »

sw.L: Nao wakamjibu malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yule aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi, wakasema, "Tumetembea huku na huko duniani, na tazama, dunia yote imetulia na [iko] kimya."
sw.B: Wakampa malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi, taarifa hii: "Tumeikagua dunia yote, na yote imetulia na iko katika amani."
sw.R: Wakamwambia malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyesimama kati ya mihadasi, "Tumezunguka dunia yote. Ulimwengu wote umetulia na uko kimya."

vi.L: Và họ đáp lời thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là vị đang đứng giữa những cây sim, rằng: "Chúng tôi đã đi qua đi lại trên đất, và kìa, cả đất đều ngồi yên và [được] nghỉ ngơi."
vi.B: Họ báo cáo với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vị đang đứng giữa những cây sim: "Chúng tôi đã đi tuần tra khắp đất, và cả đất đều yên lặng và bình an."
vi.R: Họ thưa với thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vị đang đứng giữa những cây sim: "Chúng tôi đã đi khắp đất. Cả thế giới đều êm ả và yên tĩnh."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 대답하여 말하였다. "우리가 땅을 두루 다녀 보니, 보십시오, 온 땅이 가만히 앉아 [있고] 평온합니다."
ko.B: 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 보고했다. "우리가 온 땅을 순찰했는데, 온 땅이 고요하고 평온합니다."
ko.R: 그들이 화석류나무들 사이에 서 있는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사에게 말했다. "우리가 온 땅을 두루 다녀 보았습니다. 온 세상이 조용하고 평화롭습니다."

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: the LORD's messenger, who leads the riders and speaks for Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The man among the myrtles (verses 8, 10) is now called the angel of the LORD. On this figure see the note at Genesis 16:7. Here he receives the riders' report, and in verse 12 he pleads with the LORD for Jerusalem. He appears again in 3:1-7, where he stands in judgment.

decisions.choice: all the earth sits still and is at rest: the nations are settled and undisturbed
decisions.reason: The two words describe a land at peace, with no war or unrest (Judges 3:11; Isaiah 14:7). For the nations this is good, but for Jerusalem it is not: the city lies in ruins while the world is at ease (verse 15). Haggai had spoken of a coming day when the LORD would shake the nations (Haggai 2:6-7, 21-22), and there is no sign of it yet. Darius had put down the revolts that followed his rise to power, and his empire was settled at this time.

decisions.choice: look (L); not shown (B, R); reported (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look", which marks what the riders found. Balanced and Readable say "reported" for "answered", since the riders give an account of their patrol without being asked a question.

decisions.choice: "el ángel del SEÑOR", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the published Spanish of Genesis 16:7 and Judges; the angel is the LORD's messenger and takes the divine_name setting only on "SEÑOR".

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사", without -시-; the riders report in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The angel of the LORD takes no honorific, as the term sheet sets it; the riders speak to him as to a superior.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַן מַלְאַךְ־יְהוָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עַד־מָתַ֗י אַתָּה֙ לֹֽא־תְרַחֵ֣ם אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָעַ֔מְתָּה זֶ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered [the] angel of Yahweh and said, Yahweh of hosts, until when you not will have compassion on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you have been indignant [with] this seventy years?

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered and said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not have compassion on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, with which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been indignant these seventy years?"
en.B: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been angry with these seventy years?"
en.R: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, how much longer will it be before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show compassion to Jerusalem and the towns of Judah? You have been angry with them for seventy years now."

es.L: Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} respondió y dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, ¿hasta cuándo no tendrás compasión de Jerusalén y de las ciudades de Judá, contra las cuales has estado indignado estos setenta años?».

decisions.choice: seventy years: the time of judgment Jeremiah had foretold
decisions.reason: Jeremiah said that the nations would serve the king of Babylon for seventy years, and that after seventy years God would bring his people home (Jeremiah 25:11-12; 29:10; compare 2 Chronicles 36:21; Daniel 9:2). Here the angel counts the years of God's anger with Jerusalem. From the burning of the temple in 586 BC to this vision in 519 BC was nearly seventy years, and the rebuilt temple was finished in 515 BC (Ezra 6:15), about seventy years after its destruction. The number is also a round figure for a full lifetime of judgment. 7:5 counts seventy years of fasting in the same way.

decisions.choice: how long: a lament in which the angel pleads with God for Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "How long" is the cry of the psalms of lament (Psalm 13:2-3; 74:10; 79:5). Here it is a heavenly being who speaks it for the people. The riders found the nations at ease (verse 11), so the time has come for the LORD to show mercy to his city.

decisions.choice: you have been indignant with: the LORD's anger against Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verb names hot anger, often God's anger in judgment (Malachi 1:4, of Edom; Isaiah 66:14). It is stronger than the anger of verse 2.

decisions.choice: the LORD addressed with no "O"; you with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to the LORD directly, so the name is written as a vocative with no "O", as in the Psalms, and "you" and "your" for the LORD take the setting for pronouns of God. Balanced says "hold back your compassion"; Readable makes the second clause a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: vocative "{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos", with no "oh"; God's "tu" with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to the LORD directly, as the Spanish Psalms address him, without article or "oh"; the verbs carry "you" by themselves, so only the free possessive takes the pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA wa majeshi"
decisions.reason: The Swahili vocative "Ee" before BWANA, as in the published Psalms; spans go only on the free possessive "yako", never on the verb prefixes.

decisions.choice: "Lạy CHÚA Vạn Quân"; "Ngài" for God
decisions.reason: The angel prays to the LORD with "lạy" and no "O", and speaks of God as "Ngài", as the Vietnamese prayers do; a "Ngài" that starts a sentence takes no span.

decisions.choice: "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, … 않으시겠습니까?" in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The angel of the LORD prays in 합쇼체, as the term sheet sets for this verse; "seventy years" is "70년" in figures, as Jeremiah 25:11, Daniel 9:2 and 7:5.

decisions.choice: the LORD answers the angel who talked with Zechariah
decisions.reason: The plea came from the angel of the LORD (verse 12), but the answer is given to the angel who explains the visions, who passes it on to Zechariah in verses 14-17. Zechariah does not report the LORD's words directly; he hears them through the angel.

decisions.choice: good words, comforting words: words of promise
decisions.reason: "Good words" are words that promise good, the opposite of words of judgment (Joshua 23:14-15). Jeremiah had promised, "When seventy years are completed ... I will fulfill to you my good word" (Jeremiah 29:10). The word for comfort recalls Isaiah 40:1, "Comfort, comfort my people", and verse 17 says that the LORD will comfort Zion.

decisions.choice: kind words (R)
decisions.reason: In English "good words" can mean well-chosen words. Readable says "kind words", which is close to the sense here, and keeps "words of comfort".

decisions.choice: jealous for: full of zeal for someone who belongs to me, and fiercely protective
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's passionate devotion, which will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14) and rises up to defend them (Joel 2:18, "the LORD became jealous for his land"; Isaiah 9:6, "the zeal of the LORD"). It is not envy. Here it means the LORD's burning concern for Jerusalem, which turns into anger against those who harmed her (verse 15). The same words open the promises of 8:2.

decisions.choice: call out: Zechariah is to proclaim the LORD's answer
decisions.reason: The angel tells Zechariah to proclaim aloud what the LORD has said. The message runs to the end of verse 16, and a second proclamation follows in verse 17.

decisions.choice: I have been jealous ... with great jealousy (L); deeply jealous (B); I love them and will protect them (R); the quotation marks
decisions.reason: Literal gives the verb's completed form as "I have been jealous": the LORD's zeal is not new. Balanced gives the strengthening noun as "deeply". Readable keeps "jealous" and adds what it means here, love that protects (m1), since in everyday English the word usually means envy. The angel's words are in double quotation marks, and the message Zechariah is to proclaim is in single marks inside them; it closes at the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: "celo" ("He tenido celo por ... un gran celo", L; "un celo profundo", B; "un gran celo", R)
decisions.reason: God's jealousy for his city is "celo", the zeal of Joel 2:18 and the "Dios celoso" of Exodus 20:5; "celos" would suggest envy. The angel's words open with « and the message inside them with “, as in the English; neither closes in this verse.

decisions.choice: "jaloux pour Jérusalem", "une grande jalousie"
decisions.reason: As Joel 2:18 ("jaloux pour son pays") and the "Dieu jaloux" of Exodus 20:5. The angel's words open with « and run to the end of verse 17; the message inside them takes “ ”.

decisions.choice: "wivu ... kwa ajili ya Yerusalemu"
decisions.reason: As Joel 2:18 and the "Mungu mwenye wivu" of Exodus 20:5. The angel's words open with double quotation marks and the message inside them with single marks, as the English.

decisions.choice: "nổi lòng ghen" (L), "ghen yêu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Joel 2:18 ("nổi lòng ghen", "ghen yêu"): the LORD's jealousy here is protective love for his city, not the "kỵ tà" of Exodus 20:5, which is jealousy against other gods. The angel says "ông" to Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "질투하였다" (L), "몹시 질투한다" (B), "뜨겁게 질투한다 ... 사랑하며 지켜 줄 것이다" (R)
